rv.q: Another Shot is admirable in its core message of never giving up on anyone.
But the terrific cast and peppy pacing keep things moving for 90 minutes, and there's a big enough gut-punch at the end to get some important points across.
This is too bad because Another Shot risks alienating the audience before introducing a set of characters who compellingly bear witness to the ravages of addiction.

Unfortunately, the play's episodic quality, jokey humor, and well-calculated revelations about the characters' personal lives and backstories make Another Shot seem more like a situation comedy than a finely etched character study.
The result, though from time to time impressing as a bit schematic, is what looks to be, as directed by Jackson Gay, a convincingly accurate representation of rehab’s own successes and setbacks.
Another Shot may not be a distinguished play, but it effectively provides an insider look at rehab.
Perhaps I’m wrong, but Another Shot seems too unsurprising to make much of an impact on theatergoing New Yorkers who don’t have an immediate connection to its subject.
Director Jackson Gay keeps the play teetering between denial and acceptance, and between comedy and tragedy.
Another Shot covers very familiar ground, but it's a well-crafted production that may play best to an audience of one...

cn.t: This autobiographical rehab dramedy earns mixed-positive notices for its honest portrayal of addiction and recovery, though critics note it works better when it stops trying to entertain and lets genuine emotion surface.
